title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns

facts.fact: Quality Score is measured on a scale from 1 to 10 and is available at the keyword level.
facts.quote: This score is measured on a scale from 1-10 and available at the keyword level.

facts.fact: Quality Score is calculated from three components: expected clickthrough rate, ad relevance, and landing page experience.
facts.quote: Quality Score is calculated based on the combined performance of 3 components:

facts.fact: Each Quality Score component is evaluated as 'Above average', 'Average', or 'Below average', compared with other advertisers whose ads showed for the exact same search over the last 90 days.
facts.quote: This evaluation is based on a comparison with other advertisers whose ads showed for the exact same search over the last 90 days.

facts.fact: Quality Score is based on historical impressions for exact searches of a keyword, so changing keyword match types does not impact Quality Score.
facts.quote: Quality Score is based on **historical impressions for exact searches**of your keyword, therefore changing keyword match types will not impact Quality Score.

facts.fact: Quality Score is not a key performance indicator and should not be optimized or aggregated with the rest of your data, according to Google.
facts.quote: Quality Score is not a key performance indicator and should not be optimized or aggregated with the rest of your data.

facts.fact: Quality Score is not an input in the ad auction, according to Google.
facts.quote: Quality Score is not an input in the ad auction. It’s a diagnostic tool to identify how ads that show for certain keywords affect the user experience.

facts.fact: A Quality Score of '—' in the column means there are not enough searches that exactly match the keyword to determine its score.
facts.quote: If you notice a “—” in the Quality Score column, it means there aren't enough searches that exactly match your keywords to determine a keyword’s Quality Score.

facts.fact: A broad match keyword may have a Quality Score with no impressions if a corresponding exact match keyword in the same ad group has impressions in the last 90 days.
facts.quote: A broad match keyword may have a Quality Score even though it has no impressions as long as there is a corresponding exact match keyword with impressions in the last 90 days.

facts.fact: Quality Score factors not captured include devices used in search, location of user, time of day, and assets.
facts.quote: There are factors related to your ad quality that might not be captured by Quality Score. These factors include, but are not limited to: Devices used in search, Location of user, Time of day, Assets
